subtitle.$t: This official feed from the Google Workspace team provides essential information about new features and improvements for Google Workspace customers.

content.$t:
Starting on December 02, 2026, we are updating the order of options within the "More actions" panel on Google Meet hardware touch controllers. This update introduces improvements based on usage patterns and user feedback, prioritizing high-frequency actions so room participants can access essential controls faster and with less scrolling.

Key adjustments in the panel include:

  • Moving frequently used controls such as Present, Adjust view, and People higher in the menu for direct access from the side panel on most touch controllers.
  • Retaining primary in-room actions, including Chat at the top and Control camera near the front of the list, while demoting lower-frequency tools like Recording or Streaming to streamline the menu.
  • When relevant, elevating custom room controls in spaces configured for presentations or specialized events to make meeting room management more efficient.

This change requires no additional configuration or action. End users will automatically see the refreshed menu order across supported Google Meet hardware touch devices, creating a more intuitive and consistent in-room meeting experience.



The reordered “More actions” panel on Google Meet hardware touch controllers

Getting started

  • Admins: This feature will be ON by default and cannot be disabled.
  • End users: No action is required. This update will automatically appear on supported devices.

Rollout pace

  • Early Preview devices: Gradual rollout (up to 7 days for feature visibility) starting on December 2, 2026 
  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Gradual rollout (up to 15 days for feature visibility)  starting on December 11, 2026

Availability

  • Available to all Google Workspace customers with Google Meet hardware devices

title.$t: Simplifying agent access while keeping organizations in control: MCP servers, CLI, standardized usage tiers, and admin policies

content.$t:
As AI agents transform how people work, we want to make it simple for developers to build agentic workflows while keeping organizations in control of their data in Google Workspace. We are making Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and the official Workspace CLI generally available alongside standardized usage tiers to simplify how developers build and scale agents, paired with a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum and expanded enterprise controls over AI agents.

Simplifying and securing agent access with governed Workspace MCP servers and the Workspace CLI

Developers now have two Google-managed ways to connect AI agents to Workspace without custom integration code:


  • Workspace MCP servers: Built on the open MCP standard, these Google-hosted servers let cloud and web-based AI agents securely connect to Workspace and call pre-built tools out of the box across Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat, and Tasks (with Keep coming soon). Explore supported MCP capabilities.
  • Workspace CLI: A command-line interface that brings Workspace tools directly to local environments, including developer terminals, VMs, and containerized sandboxes, for terminal-based agents. It includes packaged agent skills, dynamic command discovery, and scoped sign-in to read and update Workspace data. Explore the Workspace CLI.

Unlike traditional REST APIs, which are designed for deterministic app calls, both tools are purpose-built for dynamic agent workflows and provide:


  • Continuous improvements: Since Google fully manages these tools, agents that discover tools and schemas at runtime automatically benefit from ongoing improvements to context retrieval, credential setup, and tool accuracy.
  • Token efficiency: Rather than downloading raw data line by line via REST APIs, MCP tools return synthesized summaries within Workspace's boundary, and the CLI runs in the terminal, where agents can chain multiple tools. Both lower token costs and latency.
  • Streamlined security and compliance: Secure-by-default infrastructure with built-in user confirmations, audit logging, and admin controls helps streamline OAuth verification, Cloud Application Security Assessments, and enterprise security reviews without custom compliance work.

Standardizing the API usage tiers

In May, we announced a standardized usage model for Workspace APIs and MCP servers to give large-scale and AI tool developers a simpler, more predictable way to access higher quota while keeping Workspace infrastructure reliable for our entire community of developers.

Starting today, the Workspace APIs, including MCP servers and CLI, will have two usage tiers, starting with Gmail, Drive, and Calendar. Additional data access mechanisms will be updated similarly in the coming months.


  • Standard tier: No cost, with published usage quotas (rate limits).
  • Scaled tier: Designed for projects that need higher usage quota (rate limits).
    • Starting April 1, 2027, if you select the Scaled tier, you will be charged only for API or MCP usage above any daily free allowances. If no action is taken, your projects may be throttled to the published usage quotas.
  • MCP or CLI requirement: AI agents or similar access tools must use Workspace MCP servers or the Workspace CLI to access Workspace data, rather than calling Workspace REST APIs directly. Technical enforcement begins on February 1, 2027. Follow these steps to use MCP, and select the Scaled tier if you need higher quotas for agentic use.

Over 99% of active developers currently operate within the Standard tier and will continue to access these APIs at no additional cost. The same privacy, DLP, and data-protection standards apply across every tier.

If you are a Google Cloud Support customer, Workspace APIs will be excluded from the support variable fee calculation until at least December 2027. Any changes will be communicated with at least 90 days' notice. To understand your options, see the Google Cloud Support packages.

Keeping organizations and users in control

Making it easier for developers to connect agents to Workspace goes hand in hand with giving organizations clear oversight and control of their data. We are extending the same governance principles customers rely on across Workspace to AI agents, so admins and users can get practical control over agents that access their data:


  • Data-retention limits: Our new Workspace AI Tools Addendum prohibits using AI agents and other access tools for certain activities that could raise security risks, including storing certain data derived from use of Workspace APIs for extended periods of time, or using AI agents to scrape Workspace APIs.
  • Centralized access management: Requiring external AI agents to identify themselves in OAuth and connect through Workspace MCP servers or the Workspace CLI allows admins to manage agent access in the admin console just like traditional apps.
  • Human-in-the-loop confirmations: Routine actions like creating a draft stay seamless, while admins can set rules that prompt users to confirm sensitive actions in third-party AI tools, such as reading external files or sharing data.
  • Automatic DLP and audit logging: Existing user-level Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rules apply automatically when someone uses an AI agent, and admin audit logs record agent actions and user confirmations for clear visibility.

Over the coming months, we will roll out more granular agent policies and controls to give admins and users even finer oversight of their data.

Getting started

  • Admins
    • MCP servers, CLI, and API controls: Manage access for external AI tools, Workspace MCP servers, the Workspace CLI, and APIs; set human-in-the-loop (HITL) confirmation rules; and view agent audit logs in the Admin console under Security > API Controls. Visit the Help Center to learn more about managing access.
    • Internal-use projects: If a project is used only within your Workspace organization, administrators can mark the project as internal so higher limits remain included with your Workspace subscription. Learn more about internal-use projects.
  • Developers
    • Workspace MCP servers and CLI: Visit our configuration guides to start building with the Workspace MCP servers and Workspace CLI.
    • If you are building AI agents: Plan to switch from REST APIs to Workspace MCP servers or the Workspace CLI for agentic access before February 1, 2027, when technical enforcement begins. Review our OAuth client documentation to select Use this client for an AI-powered agent (is_agentic) on OAuth 2.0 clients used by AI agents in the Google Cloud console (traditional non-agent features should use a separate OAuth client). Review the new Workspace AI Tools Addendum.
    • Check your API usage: Use the new Workspace API usage developer dashboard to view each project’s usage against the Standard rate limits along with estimated costs. If every project is under the limits, you do not need to take any action.
    • If a project exceeds the Standard tier limits, complete one of the following steps:
      • Projects used only within your Workspace organization: Ask your Workspace administrator to mark the project as internal.
      • All other projects: Ask your Cloud Billing Admin to link a billing account and switch the project to the Scaled tier.
    • Projects that already have higher usage limits need to take the same steps as above to maintain them.
      • If no action is taken before April 1, 2027, your project limits will automatically change to Standard tier rate limits, at no additional cost.
      • For AI agents, the MCP or CLI requirement above applies first, from February 1, 2027.

Rollout pace

  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Rolling out to all in 2 weeks for the Workspace MCP servers (GA); the Google Workspace CLI (GA); Admin console agent access, human-in-the-loop (HITL), and audit log controls; the Workspace API usage developer dashboard; and Scaled tier selection.
  • MCP or CLI requirement for AI agents: Technical enforcement begins on February 1, 2027.
  • Usage limits and billing: Starting April 1, 2027, Scaled tier billing begins for the Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Drive APIs, and the Workspace CLI and MCP servers. Projects that still have higher usage limits and have not switched to the Scaled tier or been marked as internal move to Standard tier limits. Google Cloud Billing Admins and Project Owners with affected projects will receive an email with project-specific details and next steps.

Availability

  • Available to all Google Workspace customers and developers.

title.$t: New study enhancements for Flashcards in Gemini Notebook

content.$t:
We introduced three updates to flashcards in Gemini Notebook to help users better retain information, measure recall speed, and maintain consistent review routines.

  • Images: Flashcards now automatically incorporate relevant images directly from uploaded source materials, providing visual context alongside text prompts to aid comprehension.
  • Built-in stopwatch: Users can enable a stopwatch while reviewing flashcards to track time during the session, making it easier to simulate timed exam conditions.
  • Mobile study reminders: Using the Gemini Notebook mobile app, users can schedule notifications reminding them to review previously generated flashcards, supporting structured study cadences.

These capabilities help strengthen Gemini Notebook as an active learning and retention tool.

For educational institutions and enterprise organizations, these enhancements offer students, educators, and training teams a more flexible environment to prepare for exams, internal certifications, and ongoing skill development.

Getting started

  • Admins: There is no admin control for this feature. Visit the Help Center to learn more about turning Gemini Notebook on or off for users.
  • End users: Visit the Help Center to learn more about generating Flashcards in Gemini Notebook.

Rollout pace

  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Available now

Availability

  • Available to all Google Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts

Resources

  • Google Workspace Admin Help: Turn Gemini Notebook on or off for users
  • Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Flashcards or Quizzes in Gemini Notebook

title.$t: Google Meet on the web now supports sending 1080p video for all users, enabled by default

content.$t:
We’re expanding 1080p Full HD video sending in Google Meet on the web (previously limited to select paid editions) to all users. It is now enabled by default on computers with a 1080p camera and sufficient compute and bandwidth.

Meet transmits 1080p only when a participant's video tile is large enough to display it, and automatically scales resolution down when CPU or bandwidth is constrained.

Getting started

  • Admins: The default video quality can be configured at the OU or group level in the Admin console, and existing bandwidth-limit settings remain applied. Visit the Help Center to learn more about configuring default video quality.
  • End users: 1080p will be ON by default under Auto on eligible computers (unless restricted by your admin) and can be changed anytime in Settings > Video. Visit the Help Center to learn more about improving your video and audio experience.

Rollout pace

  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Extended rollout (potentially longer than 15 days for feature visibility) started on November 11, 2026

Availability

  • Available to all Google Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts.

Resources

  • Google Workspace Admin Help: Configuring default video quality
  • Google Workspace Admin Help: Manage Meet settings (for admins)
  • Google Help: Improve your video & audio experience

title.$t: Make messages in Google Chat from apps and agents easier to read with tables and headings

content.$t:
Agents and apps in Google Chat can now send messages formatted with tables and headings. Tables make it easy to compare options, share status trackers, and present data in rows and columns. Headings provide a way to separate long messages, like summaries, reports, and plans, into clear, scannable sections.

Developers can add both through the Google Chat API using standard Markdown. Headings support three levels (#, ##, and ###). Text in tables and headings can use formatting like bold, italics, links, and emoji. 

Everyone in the conversation will see tables and headings when an app or agent sends them. On the web, tables appear in the message, and you can scroll to see wider tables. On Android and iOS, tap "Show table" to see the full table. Support for viewing tables directly in the message on Android and iOS will follow. 

Tables and headings can't be created in the Chat message compose box.

Getting started

  • Admins: There is no admin control for this feature.
  • End users: There is no end user setting for this feature.
  • Developers: Chat apps can send tables and headings using standard Markdown syntax through the Google Chat API. Visit the Google Chat API documentation to learn more.

Rollout pace

  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Available now

Availability

  • Available to all Google Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts

Resources

  • Google Chat API Developers: Format messages

Building on our recent launch allowing you to view up to three time zones in Google Calendar on the web, we’re making cross-time-zone scheduling even clearer by replacing raw GMT+/- offsets (such as GMT-5 or GMT-8) with familiar, locale-aware time zone abbreviations (such as ET, CT, MT, or PT for users in the United States or MEZ in Germany). | Learn more

If selected, meeting participants will see a link to the file you are presenting displayed on the screen. | Learn more

To make it easier to send well-formatted meeting updates, share agendas, and verify Google Drive file access before sending, we’re updating the Email guests flow in Google Calendar on the web to open a native Gmail compose window directly from Calendar. | Learn more

Admins can let flows collaborate across the organization, such as sending emails, posting in Chat, and editing shared files. | Learn more

With this launch, core Workspace Studio execution and storage backends, including integrations with Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Google Meet, and Google Chat, natively adhere to assigned United States or European Union data region policies. | Learn more

Organizations no longer have to choose between the highest level of privacy and real-time collaboration. Previously, working in client-side encrypted Google Docs meant editing one user at a time. title.$t: Expanded Google Vault support for external spaces and group conversations in Google Chat

content.$t:
To give organizations more consistent visibility and help support their compliance requirements, we’re expanding Google Vault support in Google Chat. Starting mid-February 2027, Vault admins can retain, hold, search, and export messages from external spaces and group direct messages that include Workspace users from their organization. This brings these conversations to parity with how external 1:1 direct messages work today. There is no change to conversations with history off, as they are not available in Vault. 

Previously, only the organization that created an external space or group direct message could retain a copy of its messages using Vault. Now, every organization with a member in the conversation keeps its own copy: 

  • Retention and holds: Your Vault retention rules and legal holds preserve your organization’s copy of messages and attachments.
  • Search and export: You can search and export your organization’s copy in Vault. Search results for a user reflect what your organization holds, not what that user saw. Results can include previous versions of messages or deleted messages from before the user joined, if another of your users was a member at the time. 
  • Coverage period: Your organization’s copy starts when your first user joins the conversation. Existing messages are saved as they appear at that point, so edits and deletions prior to your first user joining aren’t included. From then on, new messages, edits, and deletions are saved until the last user from your organization leaves, and retained according to your retention rules and holds.

To keep the product experience consistent for participants, message visibility within the Chat UI follows the conversation creator’s retention policy. If your organization creates the conversation, your policy controls both Chat UI visibility and your copy in Vault. If an external organization creates it, their policy controls Chat UI visibility, while your policy controls your copy in Vault. Holds will apply to your copy regardless of which organization creates the conversation.

Getting started

  • Admins: This behavior is enabled automatically and applies your existing Google Chat retention rules and holds in Google Vault to your copy of messages in external spaces and group conversations your users join. While you cannot disable this Vault behavior independently, you can manage whether your users can be added to external conversations in the Admin console. Visit the Help Center to learn more about searching Google Chat messages in Vault and managing external Chat options.
  • End users: There is no end-user setting for this feature. Visit the Help Center to learn more about messaging users from other organizations in Google Chat.

Rollout pace

  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Extended rollout (potentially longer than 15 days for feature visibility) starting mid-February 2027

Availability

  • Business: Business Plus
  • Enterprise: Enterprise Standard and Plus
  • Education: Education Fundamentals, Standard, and Plus
  • Other Editions: Frontline Standard and Plus; Enterprise Essentials Plus
  • Other Add-ons: Google Vault

title.$t: Now available in beta: Collaborate in real-time on client-side encrypted (CSE) Google Docs

content.$t:
Client-side encryption (CSE) provides organizations control over access to their confidential data, with encryption that makes data indecipherable to unauthorized third-parties, including Google, and encryption keys that remain under the sole control of the customer.

Organizations no longer have to choose between the highest level of privacy and real-time collaboration. Previously, working in client-side encrypted Google Docs meant editing one user at a time. For the first time, teams can write, edit, and comment together, live, just as they would in any other Google Doc—while their content stays encrypted with keys only they control.

Eligible Google Workspace admins can sign up for the real-time collaboration beta program today, and choose to enroll their test or production domains.



Multiple users simultaneously editing and commenting in a client-side encrypted Doc

Getting started

  • Admins: This feature is available in beta to eligible customers across test and production domains. To request access, complete the real-time collaboration for CSE Docs beta registration form with your domain information. This form also outlines beta compliance details to help guide your domain selection. Once your domain is allowlisted, real-time collaboration is ON by default for newly created CSE Docs, and admins will receive onboarding and testing documentation.
  • End users: This feature is ON by default for users in domains enrolled in the real-time collaboration beta program whenever they create a new encrypted Docs. In addition, any authorized user with key access—even if their domain is not enrolled in the beta—can open, view, and collaborate in real time on existing RTC Docs shared with them. Visit the Help Center to learn more about collaborating on encrypted files.

Rollout pace

  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Available now for eligible customers enrolled in the real-time collaboration for CSE Docs beta allowlist

Availability

  • Enterprise: Enterprise Plus
  • Education: Education Standard and Plus
  • Other Editions: Frontline Plus, Assured Controls, Assured Controls Plus

  • Google Docs Editors Help: Get started with encrypted files in Drive, Docs, Sheets & Slides
  • Google Docs Editors Help: Collaborate on encrypted files in Docs, Sheets & Slides

title.$t: Google Workspace Studio support for Data Regions is now generally available

content.$t:
Google Workspace Studio now supports Data Regions, giving organizations greater governance over where their workflow data is stored at rest and processed in use. With this launch, core Workspace Studio execution and storage backends, including integrations with Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Google Meet, and Google Chat, natively adhere to assigned United States or European Union data region policies.

In addition, a dedicated Workspace Studio control has been introduced within Data Regions advanced settings in the Google Admin console. This control enables administrators to determine whether users assigned to a data region can access non-regionalized steps and generative AI capabilities, or whether those features should be restricted to keep all processing strictly in-region.

Organizations with strict regulatory, data residency, or compliance requirements can now deploy Workspace Studio automations with full assurance that data at rest and in-use processing for core services remain within their designated geographic boundaries (US or EU).

Key use cases

  • Regulated Industry Automations: Financial services, healthcare, and public sector organizations can automate administrative notifications and cross-app document workflows in Gmail, Drive, Docs, and Sheets while meeting strict regional data residency obligations.
  • Granular Policy Enforcement: Administrators can apply data region policies and advanced controls to specific organizational units (OUs) or groups, enabling localized compliance without impacting global teams.
  • Audit and Compliance Readiness: Security administrators can track and verify regional data compliance through the Security Investigation Tool (SIT).

Considerations and limitations

When an administrator configures the Data Regions advanced setting to turn off non-regionalized features for Workspace Studio (or Gemini in Google Workspace), steps that rely on multi-region processing will be deactivated:

  • Integrations: Steps connecting to non-regionalized services (such as Google Tasks, Google Forms, Gemini Notebook, Webhooks, and Drive event triggers) are greyed out in the Studio builder and blocked at runtime. 
  • AI Capabilities: Generative AI features within Studio—including AI steps, natural language flow generation, and Skills—are disabled when non-regionalized processing is turned off for Workspace Studio or for Gemini in Google Workspace. Both controls must be turned on to use generative AI features in Studio.
  • Default Experience: Users who are not covered by a Data Region policy, or whose organizational unit has non-regionalized features enabled, experience no changes to their Workspace Studio functionality.


Workspace Studio builder displaying available regionalized steps and disabled non-regionalized steps per organizational data region policy.

Getting started

  • Admins: This feature will be ON by default (features that may process data across multiple regions are enabled) and can be configured at the domain, OU, or group level under Account > Data Regions > Advanced Settings (or Data > Compliance > Data Regions > Advanced Settings). Visit the Help Center to learn more about choosing a geographic location for your data, what data is covered by a data region policy, and advanced settings for data regions.
  • End users: There is no end-user setting for this feature. For users under an organizational unit where non-regionalized features are disabled, unsupported steps and AI tools will display an explanatory banner indicating that they are unavailable due to administrative policy.


Workspace Studio configuration toggle under Data regions > Advanced settings in the Admin console.

Rollout pace

  • Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Gradual rollout (up to 15 days for feature visibility) started on November 10, 2026

Availability

  • Business: Business Standard and Business Plus  (provides in-region data storage only)
  • Enterprise: Enterprise Standard (provides in-region data storage only) and Enterprise Plus (provides in-region data storage and processing)
  • Education: Education Standard and Education Plus (provides in-region data storage only)
  • Other Editions: Frontline Plus (provides in-region data storage and processing)
  • Add-ons: Assured Controls, Assured Controls Plus, and Enterprise Data Regions

Resources

  • Google Workspace Admin Help: Data covered by data regions
  • Google Workspace Admin Help: Set up advanced settings for data regions
